panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: Overall CPU utilisation, 0-100. The per-mode breakdown in CPU Usage Breakdown is normalised differently and does not sum to this.

panels.title: Load
panels.description: System load average as reported by the metrics daemon. Compare against the core count (4 here) to judge saturation.

panels.title: Memory Usage
panels.description: Used memory, around 6.8 GB of a 16 GB host, so utilisation sits near 50%.

panels.title: Disk Throughput
panels.description: Disk read and write throughput in bytes per second. Reads peak around 160 MB/s and writes around 10 MB/s; these used to share an axis with 933 GB of used space, which made them a flat line at zero.

system.cpu.percent is the 0-100 headline already charted above. These components are per-core-normalised: they sum to roughly the core count (about 4 here), not to 100, so they show the split of busy time but cannot be read as percents of the total. iowait is the one that matters for telling CPU-bound from disk-bound.
panels.title: CPU Usage Breakdown

panels.description: Context switches are raw per second. Interrupt and softirq series are multiplied by 1000 so they share the axis; divide by 1000 for real rates (about 2,000-6,600/s).
panels.title: CPU Scheduling Activity

panels.description: Available, cached, buffers and free memory. Three of the four are large and similar, so they track each other closely; the interesting movement is in the gap between available and free.
panels.title: Memory Detail

panels.description: Used memory as a percentage. On this host it sits near 50%, which is normal for a Linux box with a large page cache.
panels.title: Memory Used Percent

panels.description: Swap allocated and free. The host runs at 100% swap used, so free sits near zero; sin/sout on Swap Page Activity shows whether it is actually being paged.
panels.title: Swap Usage

panels.description: Swap currently allocated. It reads 98-100% for long stretches, so on its own it is not a problem indicator; watch Swap Page Activity to see whether the kernel is actually paging.
panels.title: Swap Used Percent

panels.description: Pages swapped in and out per second. Any sustained non-zero value means the host is under real memory pressure, unlike the swap-used percentage.
panels.title: Swap Page Activity

panels.description: Disk busy and per-operation time, summed in milliseconds per wall-clock second. 1000 means the device was busy the entire second.
panels.title: Disk Saturation

panels.description: Host NIC throughput. Compare with the Bandwidth Usage dashboard, which measures the node's own P2P traffic; the difference is everything else on the box.
panels.title: Host Network Throughput

panels.description: All four series read zero in the live store. Any non-zero value here is worth investigating.
panels.title: Host Network Errors & Drops

panels.description: Resident set size of the node process, distinct from the host-level memory gauges. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Node Process Footprint

panels.description: Approaching the ulimit is a hard failure waiting to happen. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Open File Descriptors

panels.description: Host uptime. Reported in seconds by the collector, so it is formatted as a duration here; the value is about 709 days.
panels.title: System Uptime
